senses.gloss:
sajātīyabheda
(‘homogeneous distinction’)
------------------------------------------
According to Advaita Vedānta, ब्रह्मन्, the Absolute, is one without a second, is entirely homogeneous, and is the only Reality.
The Viśiṣṭādvaita Vedānta, however, though it accepts ब्रह्मन् as the Absolute and independent Reality, also accepts the cit (conscious entities, the jīvas or the individual souls), and the अचित् (the insentient प्रकृति or nature comprising the three guṇas) as secondary or dependent realities included in itself.
To prove the possibility of such internal distinctions, the protagonists of this school declare that bheda or distinction can be of three different kinds: vijātīya bheda (heterogeneous distinction as that of a cow from a horse); सजातीयभेद (homogeneous distinction as that of one cow from another cow); स्वगतभेद (internal distinction as between the head and the tail of the same cow).
Though ब्रह्मन् does not have the first two bhedas—because it is the only and independent Reality—it does have the third (svagatabheda).
